# Evaluating ∫ -2x⁴ sin(x) dx

I'll use **tabular integration by parts** (repeated integration by parts).

## Setting Up the Tabular Method

For ∫ x⁴ sin(x) dx, I differentiate x⁴ and integrate sin(x) repeatedly:

| Sign | Derivatives of x⁴ | Integrals of sin(x) |
|:----:|:-----------------:|:-------------------:|
| +    | x⁴               | -cos(x)             |
| −    | 4x³              | -sin(x)             |
| +    | 12x²             | cos(x)              |
| −    | 24x              | sin(x)              |
| +    | 24               | -cos(x)             |

## Combining (sign × derivative × integral)

$$\int x^4 \sin(x)\,dx = -x^4\cos(x) + 4x^3\sin(x) + 12x^2\cos(x) - 24x\sin(x) - 24\cos(x)$$

## Multiplying by −2

$$-2\int x^4\sin(x)\,dx = 2x^4\cos(x) - 8x^3\sin(x) - 24x^2\cos(x) + 48x\sin(x) + 48\cos(x)$$

## Verification (differentiating the result)

| Term | Derivative |
|------|-----------|
| 2x⁴cos(x) | 8x³cos(x) − 2x⁴sin(x) |
| −8x³sin(x) | −24x²sin(x) − 8x³cos(x) |
| −24x²cos(x) | −48xcos(x) + 24x²sin(x) |
| 48xsin(x) | 48sin(x) + 48xcos(x) |
| 48cos(x) | −48sin(x) |

All intermediate terms cancel, leaving **−2x⁴ sin(x)** ✓

<answer>2*x**4*cos(x) - 8*x**3*sin(x) - 24*x**2*cos(x) + 48*x*sin(x) + 48*cos(x) + C</answer>
